text:
Darren Raddysh came home to Toronto on a big contract after a 22-goal, 70-point season in Tampa, and 19 games in he hasn't scored. He has 44 shots, 1.99 expected goals and nothing to show for them, plus 10 assists, eight on the power play. The Leafs are leaning on him for 24 minutes a night anyway.

The scrutiny is loud. The New York Times asked whether he's living up to the deal, Toronto Hockey Daily reported Jonas Siegel questioning it, and TSN's headline had Hiller calling out a "stupid penalty" that cost the Leafs against Utah. In Tampa, Dose.ca says Charles-Édouard D'Astous has already replaced him.

Some of this should turn. His talent range centres on about 2.1 points per 60 against his current 1.3, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 99th percentile among defensemen for chances from the slot last season. Evolving-Hockey ranked him 15th among 215 defensemen at 2.6 wins, though strong Tampa teammates flattered his on-ice numbers. Our projection: 64 points. The Leafs, losers of three straight, need the first goal soon.
headline: Raddysh's big contract meets a goalless start
